notes: DESIGN MECHANISM (as required by AC#1 scout-first): SignalR exposes no native group-membership count. The chosen mechanism is OrderSubscriptionTracker — an in-memory singleton (ConcurrentDictionary<Guid,int> for viewer counts, Dictionary<string,HashSet<Guid>> for connectionId→orders). FleetHub.Subscribe calls tracker.Add(connectionId, orderId) after Groups.AddToGroupAsync; FleetHub.OnDisconnectedAsync calls tracker.RemoveConnection(connectionId). This is queryable from PickupEtaService.RefreshEtaAsync via tracker.HasViewers(orderId). VIEWER-GATED THROTTLE: PickupEtaService is a singleton service (not a BackgroundService job — the WI files_touched list had no JobsServiceExtensions.cs entry, confirming service not job design). Accept-time: BroadcastAcceptEtaAsync makes exactly 1 RouteAsync call then seeds _lastRefresh[orderId]. Position-triggered refresh: called from FleetHub.UpdatePosition for Accepted-status orders. If !HasViewers: 0 API calls, extrapolate from haversine + speed. If HasViewers but < 60s since last refresh: 0 API calls, extrapolate. If HasViewers AND >= 60s elapsed: 1 RouteAsync call, update _lastRefresh. THROTTLE PROOF: 5 min = 300s; ticks at t=30,60,90,120,150,180,210,240,270,300s (10 ticks, 30s interval). With BroadcastAcceptEtaAsync seeding lastRefresh at t=0, ticks at 60,120,180,240,300s (5 ticks) qualify → exactly 5 refresh calls, satisfying <=5 AC. ASSIGN-PICKER: The dispatcher assign-picker (GET /drivers) returns driver lat/lng for the dispatcher to compute client-side haversine distances. It does NOT call IGeoService.RouteAsync — verified by AssignPicker_UsesHaversine_ZeroRouteCalls integration test. ACCEPT INTEGRATION: AcceptEndpoint_DriverWithPosition_ExactlyOneRouteCall goes through the real HTTP endpoint (POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/accept). It seeds a driver with LastLat/LastLng set, verifies assign makes 0 route calls, and verifies accept makes exactly 1 route call (the initial driver→pickup ETA). DECISION: ETA is broadcast (SignalR group order:{orderId} -> PickupEtaUpdated message), NOT persisted. Order.DistanceM/DurationS are trip pickup→dropoff metrics set by WI-10, NOT overwritten by driver→pickup ETA. DECISION: AcceptOrderEndpoint gates the BroadcastAcceptEtaAsync call on driver.LastLat/LastLng being non-null. A driver who accepts before any GPS flush produces 0 route calls — this is acceptable per the integration test which seeds driver position. The guard avoids failing for drivers who have just gone online. BUILD: dotnet build -warnaserror exits 0 with 0 warnings. FULL SUITE: 625 passed, 4 skipped (perf tests requiring 50k seed), 0 failed. PHONE BUG FIX: Integration test uses Math.Abs(fleet.Id.GetHashCode()) % 100_000_000 formatted as 9 digits for the customer phone — avoids hex chars from Guid.ToString("N") which would fail E.164 validation.
